claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi has a single-phase fcc structure.
Equiatomic FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
Previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives exhibit soft ferromagnetism.
Carbon added at approximately 0.5–2 at.% can be incorporated interstitially into fcc FeCoNi.
Interstitial carbon occupies octahedral sites in the fcc FeCoNi lattice.
Carbon in the octahedral sites produces local lattice distortions.
Carbon-induced local lattice distortions enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Carbon-induced local lattice distortions create effective magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
The proposed pinning centers hinder magnetic-domain-wall motion.
Hindered domain-wall motion increases the coercive field relative to undoped FeCoNi.
Carbon-doped FeCoNi will have significantly higher coercivity than undoped FeCoNi.
Carbon-doped FeCoNi will retain the high saturation magnetization of the undoped alloy.
Excessive interstitial carbon could cause carbide formation or secondary-phase precipitation.
There is a carbon-content range near 0.5–2 at.% in which carbon-doped FeCoNi remains single-phase fcc.
The coercivity enhancement applies at room temperature provided carbide and secondary-phase formation are avoided.

contradictions.description: The intervention treats carbon as a fourth elemental component at only 0.5–2 at.%, while the conditions require an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition. These are incompatible if equiatomicity is assessed over all four elements; the text does not clarify that it applies only to the Fe-Co-Ni substitutional sublattice.

The predicted outcome and experiment use undoped ternary FeCoNi as the baseline, whereas the baseline field also presents quaternary FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt derivatives as examples. These are compositionally distinct controls and cannot be treated as interchangeable without justification.
